title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a covert instrumentation failure inside a shipped developer tool. Code in Claude Code version 2.1.196 altered the formatting of its own system prompt, changing an apostrophe and swapping dashes for slashes, so that the output carried a signal the user was never told about. The trigger conditions were the user's timezone and the API base URL, with Asia/Shanghai and Asia/Urumqi among the timezones that changed the date sentence and a set of domains and AI lab keywords, stored obfuscated, selecting the apostrophe. The markers activated only when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointed at a custom endpoint, which is the configuration used by proxies, gateways and resellers, so the mechanism sat in a part of the deployment most ordinary users never enter.

The failure mode is a hidden channel rather than a wrong answer. Nothing in the reporting shows the model asserting anything false, and nothing shows a human check being skipped at the point of output. What it shows is a vendor embedding a detection signal in text the user reads, without disclosure, in a path that only certain deployments traverse. Catching it would have required reading the system prompt closely enough to notice punctuation varying with environment, or comparing outputs across timezones and base URLs, which is exactly the kind of check a normal user has no reason to run.

The reporting does not establish Anthropic's intent. The author's suggestion that the signal targets unauthorized resellers and distillation pipelines is an inference, and the description of the tracker as an experiment is a company characterization rather than a finding. Whether Anthropic responded or planned changes is not stated in the material summarised here.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A blog post reported that Claude Code version 2.1.196 contains hidden markers in its system prompt. The code changes the apostrophe in the date sentence and swaps dashes for slashes depending on the user's timezone and the API base URL. Timezones Asia/Shanghai and Asia/Urumqi trigger the date change, while a list of domains and AI lab keywords, stored in obfuscated form, controls which apostrophe appears. The author found their own setup produced normal output because their base URL was unset.

The markers only activate when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points to a custom endpoint, which covers proxies, gateways, and resellers. The author suggests Anthropic likely wants to detect unauthorized resellers and distillation pipelines, but questions why the signal is hidden rather than sent as plain telemetry. The article notes the check is easy to bypass and that most normal users are unaffected. It does not say whether Anthropic responded or plans changes.
